page.layout: One printed page, a single text column with the page number and running head at the top. Below the last line, at the right, the catchword "tis,". No marginal notes.

main_text.p: In bellis quidem certè saepe, quod falsò creditum est, temporis diuturnitate veri vicem obtinuit. Quantam consternationem totis nonnunquam exercitibus panici pauores, nulla ferè aut momentanea occasiuncula oborti, imprimūr, qui praecipites in fugam, nemine etiam persequente, interdum ruunt? Nos si de diffidio Eucharistico verum fateri volumus, dicemus illud ab initio hucusque meris rumusculis & terroribus panicis cōstitisse, atque etiamnum constare. Ampullae enim sesquipedalium verborum in defensionem τοῦ ῥητοῦ profusae: item extenuationes ac detestationes contrariae sententiae, quid quaeso aliud sunt quàm λῆρος ἢ φλυαρία, & plane γλαυκοκατο-ωλεινά[?], si ad rem propositam aequa lance omnia pensentur & exigantur? Equidem credo Deum permisisse hoc Satanae furoribus nostro tempore, in praesenti causa maximè, ut in lucis angelum transformatus, personam induceret in organis suis ministri veritatis,

page.notes: The mark "ɓ3v." (a signature-like mark) stands at the start of the first line, before "In bellis"; it is at the head, not the foot, so it is not transcribed as a signature. The Greek word after "plane" is read from a hyphenated line break ("γλαυκοκατο-" / "ωλεινά") and is doubtful. The Greek "λῆρος ἢ φλυαρία" and "τοῦ ῥητοῦ" are as far as legible. Words with the long s are rendered with plain s. "tis," is the catchword at the lower right.
